question: Do the five designs score on anon-personas what they scored on syn1?
why: Mickey's action item for Yotam (recap). The 96%, the "under $1" and the 35 of 36 came from personas written by the designs' author, a design tuned on them, and prompts chosen to benefit.
hypothesis: The ranking holds (E first, D last) but E drops below 96%, because E's thresholds were fitted on syn1.
cost_estimate: about 1.2M Haiku tokens, 330 Jev requests (the test tree's estimate); anon-personas is capped at a fixed sample of 20 personas, so the estimate is an upper reading

deviations.from: test tree row: all of syn2
deviations.what: Amendment A1 replaces syn2 with anon-personas (kind real, anonymized); every bar the row puts on syn2 applies to anon-personas. syn1 stays as the reference. Yotam's decision (2026-11-10): the case runs a FIXED SEEDED SAMPLE of 20 personas from anon-personas, chosen by sorting user_ids and taking random.Random(sample_seed).sample(sorted_ids, sample_size); the sample is reproducible and pre-registered here.
deviations.cost: Running all 188 personas of anon-personas would cost about 14x the planned budget.
deviations.jev: Design E (hybrid_jev) may run on anon-personas because it is anonymized. If TYPESAFE_API_KEY or PERSONALIZATION_ALLOW_JEV=true is absent at run time, E is recorded invalid for that run and the verdict is inconclusive. Results on anon-personas are numbers only.
